source: Bereshit Rabbah 95:4
claim_en: A ROSTER IN THIS CHAPTER IS DECIDED BY A SPELLING PATTERN IN A LATER BOOK, AND THE PARTITION IS EXACT. The chain reads 'from the EDGE of his brothers he took five men' as the ones at the margin - THE WEAK - naming Reuben, Levi, Benjamin, Simeon and Issachar, because Joseph reasoned that Pharaoh would conscript the strong as his warriors. The test for who was strong is read backwards out of Moses' blessing: whoever's name is REPEATED there was mighty - Judah, Naphtali, Asher, Dan, Zebulun and Gad. MACHINE-CHECKED, AND IT HOLDS ACROSS ALL ELEVEN: counting tribe-names in Deuteronomy 33 prefix-tolerantly and filtering the homograph by morphology, exactly these six are doubled (Judah 33:7, Zebulun 33:18, Gad 33:20, Dan 33:22, Naphtali 33:23, Asher 33:24 - the three other tokens of that last name being the relative pronoun, tagged as such); Reuben, Levi, Benjamin and Issachar stand once each; and SIMEON DOES NOT APPEAR IN THE CHAPTER AT ALL, the extreme case of not-repeated. The only other doubled name is Joseph, who is not among the brothers to be presented. The chain's split of eleven into six withheld and five presented is exactly the ink's own split. METHOD RECORDED BECAUSE IT MATTERS: a naive match returned 'only one name repeats' and would have convicted the tradition - the prefixed forms hide behind the article and the preposition, exactly as at the almost-five silences.
middah: E10 (whoever's name is repeated in Moses' blessing was mighty — the eleven split, checked prefix-tolerantly)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 96:4
claim_en: A RULE ABOUT A VERB, PROVED BY THIS VERSE'S OWN NUMBER, AND IT HOLDS IN BOTH TORAH CASES. Reish Lakish takes the verb 'APPROACHED' in a death notice as a claim filed - the day itself complaining it cannot end while the man lives - and states the arithmetic rule: WHOEVER HAS 'APPROACHED' WRITTEN OF HIM DID NOT REACH HIS FATHERS' YEARS. Machine-checked on the Torah members: Jacob's ONE HUNDRED FORTY-SEVEN stands at 47:28, against Abraham's one hundred seventy-five at 25:7 and Isaac's one hundred eighty at 35:28 - short of both. Moses' one hundred twenty at Deuteronomy 34:7 stands against Amram's one hundred thirty-seven at Exodus 6:20 - short again. Two independent families, both confirmed in our own ink. THE THIRD LEG IS DECLARED UNOPENED: the king's seventy years against his forebears lies outside this Torah-only corpus.
middah: M-09 (whoever has approached written of him did not reach his fathers' years — the verb's rule, two Torah families checked)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 96:1
claim_en: A CLAIM ABOUT THE PHYSICAL LAYOUT OF THE SCROLL, UNTESTABLE IN THIS CORPUS AND CONFIRMED IN THE FULLER ONE. The chain asks why this weekly portion is CLOSED ‹סתומה› ('setuma') - the only one with no open space before it - and gives three answers: because with Jacob's death the enslavement began and their eyes were closed; because he sought to reveal the end of days and it was SEALED from him; and because he was shielded from the world's troubles in those years. OPENED, AND THE VERDICT SPLITS BY TEXT LAYER. In THIS corpus the machine is SILENT: we carry cantillation only - every mark tagged disjunctive or conjunctive - and no section-break markers at all, so there is no white space here to measure. In the canonical Tanakh text layer, which carries the Masoretic section markers themselves (1,981 samekh and 1,181 pe across the Tanakh, 92 of them in Genesis), THE CLAIM CONFIRMS with an eleven-of-eleven control: of the twelve Genesis portions, the eleven that have a preceding verse were checked, TEN carry a section marker on that verse (seven open, three closed) - and VAYECHI ALONE HAS NONE, its preceding verse 47:27 carrying its verse-end mark and nothing else. The zero is a real zero, not a data gap: the verse does bear marks, just no section break, and the control verse 44:17 carries an open marker in the same table. The tradition's OBSERVATION is exact; its three REASONS are a separate question the ink does not touch.

check.note: A scribal-layout claim: untestable in this corpus, which holds cantillation only; confirmed against the canonical text layer's Masoretic section markers, where Vayechi alone among the book's portions begins with no break.

middah: ink (the closed portion — no section marker before it, confirmed in the fuller text layer)

source: Bereshit Rabbah 96:3
claim_en: AUTHORITY EBBING AT THE END, CENSUSED IN THREE CASES, ONE OF THEM VISIBLE IN THE INK ITSELF. Against 'no man rules the spirit, and there is no dominion on the day of death,' three instances are recorded: Moses' own trumpets sequestered so that another could not sound them, so that he had to summon the elders by word; Pinhas acting before Moses at Shittim; and a king demoted in the writing - 'the time for DAVID to die approached,' not 'for KING David,' the title dropped as the dominion goes. So too here, where the patriarch lowers himself before his own son: 'if I have found favor in your eyes.' The machine's state change at this verse is that the father becomes a petitioner to his child. THE THIRD CASE'S INK IS OUTSIDE THIS CORPUS and is carried on the chain's authority, not confirmed here.

check.note: A three-case census of authority declining at death, the third resting on a title dropped in a book outside this corpus.

middah: plain (a teacher's statement — an identification, a narrative expansion, a recorded dispute, or the verse's own wording read as the rule; no catalogued inference form)

source: Onkelos Genesis 47:22; Onkelos Genesis 47:26
claim_en: THE BLOCK'S ONE PERMANENT LEGISLATIVE ACT, AND THE TRANSLATION KEEPS ITS EXEMPTION EXACT. The famine economy ends in a statute: the fifth belongs to Pharaoh, and Onkelos renders it as a STANDING OBLIGATION they must give, while preserving the exemption word for word - only the land of the priests he did not buy, and the fifth does not touch it. The text says the law stands 'to this day,' which makes this the one act in the block that survives the story as law rather than as event. A tax with a religious exemption, written into a narrative and reported as still in force.

check.note: A famine economy ending in a permanent tax statute with a priestly exemption, rendered by the translation as a standing obligation.

middah: ink (the received translation's rendering)

source: Onkelos Genesis 47:21
claim_en: THE POLICY'S SHAPE IS DECIDED IN TRANSLATION, AT THE VERSE WHERE THE ANCIENT VERSIONS DIVIDE. 'He moved the people TO THE CITIES, from one end of Egypt's border to the other' is rendered 'he transferred them FROM CITY TO CITY' - a rotation of populations rather than an urbanization. This is the standing crux of the chapter, where the versions part company, and the received translation votes for population transfer. Whether the administration urbanized a countryside or shuffled it is not a detail: it decides what the unit's resettlement operator models.

check.note: A resettlement clause rendered as city-to-city transfer rather than urbanization, at the verse where the ancient versions divide.

source: Onkelos Genesis 47:31

source: Bereshit Rabbah 96:5
claim_en: THE BURIAL REQUEST OF THIS BLOCK CARRIES A DOCTRINE READ AT ITS NEIGHBOUR. 'Do not bury me in Egypt' at 47:29-30 is where the four reasons land - the dust destined to become lice, the fear of being made an object of worship with the rule that punishment reaches the worshipped as the worshipper, the refusal to let Egypt earn merit, and the land doctrine with its tunnels for the righteous buried abroad. Read in the previous block's ledger against its anchor and back-credited to its home verses here. The oath at the bed is what the last three units' burial operators execute.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 40:6; Bereshit Rabbah 86:2
claim_en: TWO STANDING MACHINES CLOSE THEIR GENESIS BUSINESS IN THIS BLOCK. The paved-way table takes its THIRD seat of this sweep at 47:4 - 'we have come TO SOJOURN in the land' matching the first patriarch's own sojourning verb, and Onkelos renders it 'to dwell TEMPORARILY,' writing the pairing's sense into the verse. And the descent decree, which held that Jacob was liable to be brought down IN CHAINS and was instead drawn down by his son, is executed here in its softened form: settlement in the best of the land, by royal grant. A punishment recorded as commuted, and the commutation is this block's event.

check.note: A typological table taking a third seat and a decree of forced descent executing in a softened form, both closing on this block's verses.

middah: E7 (to-sojourn at 47:4 matching the first patriarch's sojourn — the paved-way pair; the commuted descent decree beside)
